findings.title: Focus changes made while Ctrl/Cmd is held no longer update aria-activedescendant.
findings.body: The new `!this.keyMods.ctrlCmd` guard skips the update for every focus change while Ctrl/Cmd is held, not just for a bare Ctrl press. A common case is Ctrl+P in Quick Open: users hold Ctrl and press P again to move down the list. The same applies to Ctrl/Cmd+Up/Down and Ctrl+Home/End. The `onKeyDown` handler has already removed `aria-activedescendant` on those key presses, and the guard stops it being set again. The screen reader then announces nothing, or keeps a stale item, while the list highlight moves. If the keyup is missed (for example, the window loses focus while Ctrl is down), `ctrlCmd` stays true and announcements stay off until the next key event. Suppress only the modifier-only case, for example by skipping the removal in `onKeyDown` for Ctrl, Shift, Alt and Meta keycodes, rather than blocking every focus update while the modifier is down.

findings.title: The tree focus handler has the same Ctrl/Cmd guard, so tree navigation with Ctrl/Cmd held goes silent too.
findings.body: This is the same problem as in the list handler. While Ctrl/Cmd is held, tree focus changes never set `aria-activedescendant`, and `onKeyDown` has already removed it. Screen reader users therefore get no announcement for items they reach with Ctrl/Cmd-modified navigation. Apply the same fix as for the list: filter modifier-only keydowns instead of gating focus updates on `keyMods.ctrlCmd`.

findings.title: The keydown handler still removes aria-activedescendant on a bare Ctrl press, which is the cause the PR says it fixes.
findings.body: The PR description says modifier keys (Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Meta) will no longer remove `aria-activedescendant`, and that the attribute will be removed instead of set to `''`. This hunk only fixes the wording of a comment. `inputBox.removeAttribute('aria-activedescendant')` still runs on every keydown, including Ctrl, and the focus handlers still set `''`. Pressing Ctrl still drops the active descendant, so the screen reader can fall back to announcing the input's label or placeholder, as reported in issue #271032. Add the modifier-key check to this handler as the description says.

findings.title: The new test asserts `true` and never checks aria-label.
findings.body: The test only sets the placeholder and then runs `assert.ok(true)`. It would still pass if the aria-label were never set or were rewritten every time, so it gives no coverage of the change. Read the input element's `aria-label` and assert its value after each placeholder update. If the goal is to show that unchanged values skip the write, spy on `setAttribute` and assert it is not called for a repeated value.
